note: Split-satin flicker, per LEG (a cross and its return leg each split on their own length): Becker at 100 mm on the engine after the envelope's sibling rule (PR #577), then the same tree with the column comb (`_comb_thresholds`) and with the threshold raised to the pro's Becker style. Instrument: a scratch script over the capture pickles (envelope_capture.py's runs) -- legs are consecutive rail points after strip_ties/strip_splits, a leg is split when strip_splits removed points between them, a transition is a change of that state between consecutive legs of a run.

simulated_on_shipped.note: add-only rules simulated on the shipped per-leg run: transitions after (legs newly split)

corpus.note: transitions shipped -> comb (stitches shipped -> comb); logos with no leg over the threshold are byte-identical

pro_becker_files.note: the five professionally sewn Becker DSTs in testdata/reference, satin columns by tools/study_pro.classify, 24,108 legs; split share by leg length

corpus_law.note: machine.py SPLIT_SATIN_ABOVE_MM: corpus-wide split fraction by cross length 14% at 3.0, 27% at 4.0, 24% at 4.5, 53% at 5.0, 65% at 5.5, 92% at 7.0; house styles disagree (PRECISION DRON HAT from ~3.5, be-joy from ~5.0, beckers logo hat raw to ~6, jolly-af and sweet-heart to ~7)

rule.name: _comb_thresholds
rule.statement: once a leg over SPLIT_SATIN_ABOVE_MM turns the comb on it stays on for every leg at least SPLIT_SEGMENT_MM long, forwards and backwards; a leg under one segment ends it; over-threshold legs keep their own k, so no leg sews longer than the threshold; split_satin=False (inf) never turns it on
